core.name: Correlation

core.name: eidetic memory

confusables.reason: Proactive interference is a memory-forgetting concept, tempting because the scenario involves memory, but it concerns old memories disrupting new ones rather than vivid visual recall.

confusables.name: retroactive interference
confusables.reason: Retroactive interference is a near-miss forgetting concept in the same memory domain, but it describes new learning disrupting old memories, not photographic recall.

items.notes: The item tests eidetic memory as vivid, enduring visual recall; interference and intelligence options are unrelated distractors.

core.name: test-retest reliability
core.evidence: His three scores were very similar to one another. This similarity suggests that the test has

supporting.name: reliability
supporting.evidence: His three scores were very similar to one another.

confusables.name: split-half reliability
confusables.reason: Split-half reliability is another form of reliability, so it is tempting when the stem asks about consistency, but it concerns internal consistency between halves of one administration, not similarity across repeated administrations.

confusables.name: content validity
confusables.reason: Content validity is a validity concept in the same testing domain, but it concerns whether a test covers the full range of material, not score consistency over time.

confusables.name: validity
confusables.reason: Validity is the other major testing quality and is easily confused with reliability, but construct validity concerns whether a test measures the intended construct, not repeated-score similarity.

items.notes: The item tests test-retest reliability: similar scores across repeated administrations. Split-half reliability and validity options are the narrow-domain confusables.
